newsitem.title: USA: US adj retail sales up 1.7 pct w/e July 5-Redbook.
newsitem.headline: US adj retail sales up 1.7 pct w/e July 5-Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 1.7 percent in fiscal June versus last month, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.

The index rose 8.3 percent compared with the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales advanced 8.3 percent in the fifth and final week of June, ended July 5, compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
June sales ended on a reasonably positive note, maintaining the renewed strength seen in the previous week after relative slippage mid-month, reported an analyst at Redbook Research.

Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Redbook Research, said that regional department stores registered modest improvements, while national department stores reported some weakness in sales, specifically in home furnishings.
Warm weather helped to boost sales for the month, enabling retailers to push out seasonal inventory, he said.
"(Retailers) were still playing catch-up from the cool spring, so they were able to sell the seasonal merchandise," said Eilenberg in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Looking ahead, retailers will not have to rely on heavy markdowns to keep retailers in the stores, Eilenberg said.
Since overall June sales were relatively robust, retailers are not expected to slash prices drastically to lure consumers, he said.
"There is not going to be a merchandise hangover ... it's planned clearance more than panic clearance," Eilenberg added.
